answer: A practical defence is Invested wildlife rehabilitator permit with wildlife trust attestation. It rests on a permit the trust renews after release audits, which gives every honest agent a bridge that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. What the farm fears is not one hard check but a check that cannot be shared: a permit the trust renews after release audits is per-account by construction, and the canyon is that the tenth clone costs as much as the first. Each clone pays the full price again — no bulk discount, no shared proof — and the gale is exactly why the farm stays small or goes broke.
